section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1978
title: PART-I ACCIDENTAL DEATHS IN INDIA ACCIDENTAL DEATHS A total of 118594 accidental deaths were recorded by the Police in India during 1978 compared with the figures of 117338 (+1·I) in 1977 and 111611 (+6·3) in 1976. Volume of Accidental Death per lakh of population: A study of the figures would show that accidental deaths in India recorded an increasing trend from 1971 to 1978 except for 1976 when the total number of accidental deaths came down to 111611 from 113016 in 1975 and again registered an upward trend registering total number of accidental deaths 117338 in 1977 and 118594 in 1978. The volume of accidental deaths per lakh of population has shown a mixed trend during 1971 to 1978 and it ranged between 19·2 for 1971 to 18·2 for 1976 in spite of the fact that the population of India has shown an increasing trend from 1971 to 1978 continuously. The details regarding the number of year-wise accidental deaths and volume of accidental deaths per lakh of population for the period 1971-1978 are set forth in Table-I. columns.name: Volume of Accidental deaths per lakh of population
header: Volume of Accidental deaths per lakh of population

notes: The total accidental deaths reported during 1978 have been classified under two broad categories: (A) accidental deaths due to natural causes, like lightning, heat stroke and land slide etc. and (B) accidental deaths due to other causes like mishaps in factories, railway accidents, air crashes and boat capsize etc. Category ‘A’ accounted for 4·5 percent of total accidental deaths recorded in 1978 in comparison to 10·1 percent in 1977. Under this category, the maximum number of deaths was reported by ‘Lightning’ (2177) followed by ‘Floods’ (1208), Heat Strokes (664), ‘Land Slides’ (619), Cyclone’ (410) and ‘Cold and Exposure’ (267). Category ‘B’ claimed 95·5 percent of the total accidental deaths registered during 1978 against 89·9 percent registered during 1977. Under this category the maximum number of accidental deaths were recorded under the head ‘Drowning’ (25623) followed by accidents ‘On Roads’ (17660), ‘By Fire’ (11187), ‘In Railways’ (11117), ‘Poisoning’ (6438), ‘Animal Bitting/Killing’ (3816), ‘Fire Arms’ (1707), ‘House Collapse’ (1476), ‘Mines and Quarry Disaster’ (798), ‘Boat Capsize’ (399), ‘Explosion’ (340), ‘Air-Crashes’ (133) and ‘Miscellaneous Causes’ (32064). Only Drowning shared 21·6 percent of the total accidental deaths in India during 1978 followed by accidents on Road (14·9%), ‘By Fire’ (9·5%) and ‘In Railways’ (9·4%) while 27·0 percent were shared by all other miscellaneous causes.
